 ‘Lanterns’ Showrunner Chris Mundy Reacts To DC Studios Shake-Up: “We Thought Everything Had Settled”
 By Christopher Marc 
 November 10, 2026 9:05 am 
 0 
 69 
 Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp 
 Yesterday, news of the big exit of James Gunn and Peter Safran from DC Studios shocked a lot of people after there had been some assurances made by David Ellison / Skydance that the two would keep their creative positions post-merger, only to be replaced by Jeremy Latcham (a former Marvel Studios executive producer, whose last superhero film credit was “ Spider-Man: Homecoming ” in 2017).
 READ MORE: Skydance Expected To Dismantle James Gunn & Peter Safran’s DC Universe Plans Following Their Firing 
 That shock and mostly confusion isn’t just relegated to the press and audience. The Playlist’s very own Gregory Ellwood was in attendance to hear “Lanterns” co-creator/co-showrunner Chris Mundy speak on Monday during the show’s FYC event in Westwood, California. He was able to get a quote from the DCU creative about the studio’s unclear future and how this all may/may not impact a second season.
 When Ellwood directly asked Mundy if the big shakeup could help “Lanterns” Season 2 move forward sooner, the response wasn’t exactly enthusiastic: “We thought everything had settled [after the merger]. I can imagine a world where everyone retreats to their corners, but then, you know, it’s a coin flip, 50/50.”
 Obviously, there is a lot of uncertainty involved here, and despite Mundy/ HBO Max quietly getting a Season 2 writers’ room together (a greenlight has yet to be announced, mind you), what exactly happens when talk is arising about a DCU-wide reboot from Skydance brass or a soft reboot sounds a little ominous for a project’s future like “Lanterns.” If you didn’t already know, the show was going to be directly tied into Gunn’s “ Man of Tomorrow ” next summer ( Aaron Pierre ‘s John Stewart crossing over with Superman and the Justice Gang sounded like a great way to follow up the show). 
 Support independent movie journalism to keep it alive. Sign up for The Playlist Newsletter. All the content you want and, oh, right, it’s free .
 In theory, could “Lanterns” keep chugging along without direct ties to future feature films? Yeah, sure. But how exactly would that benefit a larger cinematic universe, or would Skydance revert to a pre-Snyderverse policy of treating DC movies as standalone universes/franchises instead of one piece of connective tissue? Lots of questions, but not many answers yet.
